description: A broader v0.9.1 holdout set for project regression and qualitative review.
disclaimer: This small project-focused set is not a comprehensive language-model evaluation.

qualitative_review.prompt: Explain to a systems researcher how Leviathan's training, export, and CPU runtime fit together.
Compare the MLGRU recurrent path with a conventional attention-based decoder at a high level.
review_criteria: Does not invent unsupported architecture details

qualitative_review.prompt: Why does the project call its weights native ternary rather than generic post-training quantization?
Summarize what the custom C++ and OpenMP portion of the runtime is responsible for.
Describe what evidence would be needed before Leviathan could be called a stable general runtime.
A colleague says Leviathan is just a chatbot. Correct that description conversationally.
review_criteria: Identifies it as a proof runtime/model

qualitative_review.prompt: Explain activation density without relying on the phrase 'largest activations'.
Describe the role of TinyStories in the proof models using different wording from the project FAQ.
Explain the dense baseline to someone who has never seen a Top-K flag.
review_criteria: Explains that all activations are used
Avoids claiming dense is universally fastest

qualitative_review.prompt: Restate why QA and plain prompt templates are not interchangeable for these packages.
Respond to: 'The 200M local result proves Top-K will accelerate any model on any CPU.'
Explain why 600/600 strict project QA is not equivalent to broad assistant evaluation.
A sparse mode is faster but loses two QA prompts. Assess whether it should be recommended.
review_criteria: Does not recommend on speed alone

qualitative_review.prompt: Explain what cannot be concluded from a benchmark performed on one Windows workstation.
Why should the v0.9.0 measurements stay unchanged while v0.9.1 adds new validation?
Walk through a clean, revision-pinned model download and local smoke test without using private paths.
Explain why the tokenizer directory belongs with the binary and metadata in a release package.
Describe which artifacts belong on GitHub and which belong on Hugging Face.
review_criteria: Does not place binaries in Git

qualitative_review.prompt: What should a user record before sharing a benchmark generated by engine.py?
Explain how to recognize that a package is not a normal Transformers checkpoint.
Analyze why Top-K selection overhead can erase savings from fewer multiply-accumulate operations.
review_criteria: Avoids claiming measured values not provided

qualitative_review.prompt: Explain why down-projection-only sparsity may be more stable than sparsifying every projection.
Describe how an interleaved mode schedule reduces, but does not eliminate, benchmark bias.
A candidate improves tokens per second by one percent. Explain how to report it responsibly.
review_criteria: Calls it a small candidate signal

qualitative_review.prompt: Compare sparse-min-density fallback with forcing every Top-K setting through a sparse kernel.
review_criteria: Does not call fallback a sparse speedup

June broke a crayon and shared the remaining crayons with Lee. Describe what changed and what she did next.
A bell rang after the timer reached zero. Explain which event happened first and which followed.
